endpoints.reach: Skillet Creek Access to North Fraser Ramp
endpoints.coordinateEvidenceDetail: ia_dnr_boone_fraser_ramp_water_entries d0c93815-4d00-449c-823e-41c5ea788468: The official Boone County water-trail map identifies North Fraser and South Fraser as the concrete-ramp endpoints of the constructed portage around the Fraser low-head dam. Coordinates come from the matching Iowa DNR public water-access inventory features. Each inventory point was independently checked against current Esri World Imagery and coincides with the water-side end of the visible ramp, so it is retained as the water entry rather than projected to a mid-river flowline. North Fraser is visibly on the river even though the current NHD water polygon ends about 103 feet away; that known hydrography offset is preserved below.
endpoints.note: Stored coordinate matches the exact named authoritative water-entry control (ia_dnr_boone_fraser_ramp_water_entries d0c93815-4d00-449c-823e-41c5ea788468) on Des Moines River; the 316 ft named-flowline offset reflects incomplete or generalized NHD coverage, not a proposed coordinate move.

endpoints.reach: Skillet Creek Access to North Fraser Ramp
endpoints.coordinateEvidenceDetail: ia_dnr_webster_skillet_creek_access_261_20260918 1fed8473-4f35-4ee6-a833-a95328b2d6d4: Iowa DNR's public water-access feature 25 identifies Skillet Creek Access 261 on the Des Moines River in Webster County, with a natural 9-by-53-foot access and parking 31 feet away. The state Des Moines River Water Trail map labels this site as access 261 and defines access numbers as rounded river miles; the DNR guide names the 15.5-mile Deception Hollow-to-Skillet reach. Use the GIS point 42.26169114946014,-93.99540928857351 as the official access-site anchor. The precise wet toe is not surveyed.
endpoints.note: Stored coordinate matches the named authoritative access-area control (ia_dnr_webster_skillet_creek_access_261_20260918 1fed8473-4f35-4ee6-a833-a95328b2d6d4) on Des Moines River; this confirms the public access site, not the exact water-edge point. Confirm the water-edge location and carry before paddling.
